assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains the horizon, flatness and relic problems and, through the quantum origin of density fluctuations, supplies the seeds of cosmic structure. This is among the most consequential ideas in modern cosmology, and the nearly scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum was later tested with remarkable precision by CMB and large-scale-structure data. As a theorist in high-energy physics and cosmology I regard this as a case where theory made predictions that nature then supported.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the inflationary scenario, Linde supplied the new/chaotic inflation that made it viable, and Mukhanov computed the quantum generation of perturbations. These are three distinct, decisive contributions that fit a three-person prize. The longlist does not credit Starobinsky or others who contributed early (for example de Sitter-phase models and fluctuation calculations), so the fairness of this configuration is open; I am recalling the history from memory and have not verified details here.
assessment.maturity: Strongly timely: the CMB acoustic peaks, near scale invariance and Gaussianity agree with the inflationary picture, and the precision data are decades old. Independent confirmation of the fluctuation spectrum is strong, but the inflationary mechanism itself, as distinct from its predictions, is not uniquely established.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial gravitational waves, so the energy scale and specific model remain unconstrained.
Priority disputes over who first formulated inflation and the fluctuation calculation could complicate the configuration.
Whether alternatives to inflation can reproduce the same observations is still argued, and some conceptual problems (initial conditions, eternal inflation, measure) remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies opened neutrino astronomy and was a genuine discovery in nature rather than a model. Follow-up associations with TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, and the measurement of the spectrum, give the result clear and lasting scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit names only Francis Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube from the start and championed the kilometre-scale detector. A single-laureate award would leave out other leaders of the IceCube collaboration and builders of predecessor instruments (AMANDA); how credit should be shared with them is not resolved by the supplied record, and I cannot add them beyond the credited name.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: the diffuse flux has been confirmed with multiple event topologies and analyses, and a cubic-kilometre instrument is an established facility. Source identification is still at an early stage.
uncertainties: The sources of the bulk of the flux are not yet identified.
Attribution rests on one credited name for a large collaboration, so a prize configuration may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Z2 topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new classification of band insulators and opened a major field. The theory is conceptually deep and was followed by clear experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells with helical edge conduction, so this is a case of theory with strong empirical clues from nature.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction of the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp led the experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells. The three-person configuration is natural, although Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realization, and that omitted credit may be contested. I am relying on memory for the details.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent experiments in HgTe, in 3D materials such as Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 by ARPES, and a long record of follow-up work confirm the concept. Recognition is timely and stable.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and for the 3D materials discoveries is not captured in the supplied names.
Whether the nominated experiment (conductance quantization) is judged clean enough relative to ARPES work on 3D topological insulators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced full-sky CMB maps that fixed the main cosmological parameters to percent-level precision, giving the Lambda-CDM concordance model, measuring a flat universe and reionization optical depth. This is observational cosmology with a lasting impact on the field I follow closely.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the WMAP mission as principal investigator, Page was a leading instrument and observational scientist, and Spergel led the analysis and cosmological interpretation. The configuration is plausible but the WMAP team was large and Wilkinson and others were involved. Since COBE was recognized in 2006 and Planck followed WMAP, the committee would need to decide whether WMAP's contribution is sufficiently distinct as a new discovery.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and independently confirmed by Planck and ground-based experiments. The case for timeliness is weaker, since the principal results date from 2003 to 2012 and the field's central discoveries have already been recognized in part (COBE 2006, 2019 cosmology prize).
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier COBE recognition and with the 2019 cosmology prize may make the incremental discovery seem less distinct.
Planck's later and superior results may dilute the case for singling out WMAP.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a large theta-13 from reactor antineutrino disappearance was a clean, decisive discovery that completed the three-flavour mixing picture and opened a path to leptonic CP violation searches. Its importance is high even though it follows the neutrino-oscillation prize of 2015.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang as spokesperson/lead, Luk as co-spokesperson) and RENO (Kim) are the named credited leaders; Double Chooz is not credited. Attribution to collaboration leaders is workable but the dependence on large teams and competing nearly simultaneous results complicates credit. I recall that Daya Bay and RENO reported within weeks of each other in 2012; this is not verified here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple reactor experiments and accelerator results agree on the value, and the measurement is now a precision input.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views a leading-leader configuration for large collaborations as fair, and the exclusion of Double Chooz and T2K contributions.
The scientific novelty after 2015 recognition of oscillations may be judged more incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of magic-angle flat bands and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. The idea is original and the experiments showed that the theory identified a real, tunable platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction of the magic angle and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. The credited trio is natural. Cao and Fatemi, who did much of the experimental work, are not credited, and other theoretical work (for example Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) preceded it; these allocations remain debatable.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: observations have been reproduced by many groups and the field is very active, but the mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled and the discovery is relatively recent.
uncertainties: The nature of the superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated.
Credit to earlier theory and to the experimental co-first authors is unresolved.
The case may be premature relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution connected quantum foundations to practical information security, and the protocols (BB84, E91) are conceptually important and have inspired a field. It builds on ideas close to the entanglement-based experiments honoured in 2022.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 and Ekert proposed the entanglement-based protocol, making this a natural three-person configuration. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea and other contributions might need acknowledgement but Wiesner is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually mature and experimentally demonstrated over fibre and satellite links, though its practical security and deployment remain contested. The physics discovery is secure, while the engineering impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Practical security against implementation attacks limits real-world impact.
Whether this is judged physics (as opposed to information science) in the committee's framing.
Overlap in spirit with the 2022 prize may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice quantum simulation realized Hubbard-type models with ultracold atoms, enabling the observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and later microscopic control and study of many-body dynamics. It opened a rich field at the interface of atomic physics and condensed-matter theory.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac provided the theoretical proposals, Bloch and Greiner carried out the pioneering experiments, and Dalibard is also credited; a fair allocation among five names is difficult, and I choose three, which leaves out other significant contributors. The overlap with other nominated atomic and quantum-computing entries also complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many groups have reproduced and extended the results. Recognition is plausible but the quantum-gas field has partly been recognized by earlier prizes (1997, 2001, 2012).
uncertainties: Credit is spread over five credited names and the selection of three is contestable.
Potential overlap with other candidates built on the same Zoller and Cirac proposals.
Many of the claims for scientific advantage over classical computation are still developing.
